title: Dynamic factor models
text: compare three models known loadings, simulate six series three AR(1) trends. Trend 1 strongly autocorrelated (ϕ1=0.85\phi_1 = 0.85) drives series 1 3. Trend 2 weakly autocorrelated (ϕ2=0.15\phi_2 = 0.15) drives series 4 5. Trend 3 (ϕ3=0.55\phi_3 = 0.55) largest innovation SD drives series 6 alone. hold last 15 80 time points. mvgam_data() checks training data plots series, held-data black: six simulated series. Series 1 3 follow one trend, series 4 5 second, series 6 third. Black lines dashed line held-data.
code: set.seed(3)  n_time <- 80 n_series <- 6 n_lv <- 3 n_train <- 65 phi_true <- c(0.85, 0.15, 0.55) sig_true <- c(0.5, 0.35, 0.8)  # Each trend starts at its stationary distribution lv <- matrix(NA, n_time, n_lv) lv[1, ] <- rnorm(n_lv, 0, sig_true / sqrt(1 - phi_true^2)) for (t in 2:n_time) {   lv[t, ] <- phi_true * lv[t - 1L, ] + rnorm(n_lv, 0, sig_true) }  # Series 1-3 load on trend 1, series 4-5 on trend 2, series 6 on trend 3 Z_true <- matrix(0, nrow = n_series, ncol = n_lv) Z_true[cbind(1:6, c(1, 1, 1, 2, 2, 3))] <- 1  # Observations add Gaussian noise with SD 0.2 y_mat <- lv %*% t(Z_true) +   matrix(rnorm(n_time * n_series, 0, 0.2), n_time, n_series)  sim_data <- data.frame(   time = rep(seq_len(n_time), n_series),   series = factor(     rep(paste0("s", seq_len(n_series)), each = n_time),     levels = paste0("s", seq_len(n_series))   ),   y = as.numeric(y_mat) ) train <- sim_data[sim_data$time <= n_train, ] test  <- sim_data[sim_data$time >  n_train, ] mvgam_data(train, family = gaussian(), trend_formula = ~ AR(),            newdata = test)

Counts along route surveyed effort EtE_t Poisson mean λtEt\lambda_t E_t, effort entering term offset(log_effort). occupancy survey plot area AA detects species least one individual present. Poisson number individuals plot, detection probability pt=1−exp⁡(−λtA)p_t = 1 - \exp(-\lambda_t ). inverse complementary log-log link, cloglog(pt)=log⁡λt+log⁡\text{cloglog}(p_t) = \log \lambda_t + \log (McCullagh Nelder 1989). bernoulli(link = "cloglog"), occupancy record shares log-intensity counts, offset log⁡\log . Opportunistic sightings arrive rate λt\lambda_t thinned unknown, constant observer effort. treat thinned Poisson process, whose intercept absorbs unknown thinning. shape ff can still estimated sightings (Fithian et al. 2015; Renner et al. 2015).
code: set.seed(2026) n_t <- 96 env <- as.numeric(scale(cumsum(rnorm(n_t, 0, 0.3)))) f_env <- function(x) 1.5 * exp(-0.5 * (x - 0.4)^2) - 0.4  z <- numeric(n_t) for (t in seq_len(n_t)) {   z[t] <- rnorm(1, 0, 0.35) +     (if (t > 1) 0.55 * z[t - 1] else 0) +     (if (t > 12) 0.30 * z[t - 12] else 0) } lambda <- exp(0.5 + f_env(env) + z)  effort <- runif(n_t, 0.5, 2) area <- 0.25 log_thinning <- -0.8  idm_data <- data.frame(   time = seq_len(n_t),   series = factor("species1"),   env = env,   log_effort = log(effort),   count = rpois(n_t, lambda * effort),   pa = rbinom(n_t, 1, 1 - exp(-lambda * area)),   po = rpois(n_t, lambda * exp(log_thinning)) )  # The count route ran for the first two years only. Later months carry # unit effort, which makes their hindcasts expected counts per unit # effort unsurveyed <- idm_data$time > 24 idm_data$count[unsurveyed] <- NA idm_data$log_effort[unsurveyed] <- 0

Detection rises 0.05 logit scale day camera deployed. cameras run 60 80 months. three simulated monitoring records. camera record gaps months cameras run.
code: set.seed(2024) n_time <- 80 z <- numeric(n_time) z[1] <- rnorm(1, 0, 0.4 / sqrt(1 - 0.7^2)) for (t in 2:n_time) {   z[t] <- 0.7 * z[t - 1] + rnorm(1, 0, 0.4) }  month <- (seq_len(n_time) - 1) %% 12 + 1 log_effort <- log(runif(n_time, 0.8, 1.2)) deploy_days <- runif(n_time, 5, 20) mu_biomass <- exp(0.5 + sin(2 * pi * month / 12) + z)  mv_data <- data.frame(   time = seq_len(n_time),   series = factor("pop1"),   month = month,   log_effort = log_effort,   deploy_days = deploy_days,   count = rpois(n_time, exp(1.5 + log_effort + z)),   biomass = rgamma(n_time, shape = 2, rate = 2 / mu_biomass),   camera = rbinom(n_time, 1, plogis(-0.5 + 0.05 * deploy_days + z)) ) mv_data$camera[-sort(sample.int(n_time, 60))] <- NA observed <- do.call(rbind, lapply(c("count", "biomass", "camera"), function(r) {   data.frame(time = mv_data$time, value = mv_data[[r]], response = r) })) observed$response <- factor(observed$response,                             levels = c("count", "biomass", "camera")) ggplot(observed, aes(time, value)) +   geom_line(data = ~ subset(.x, response != "camera"), colour = "#A25050") +   geom_point(size = 1, na.rm = TRUE) +   facet_wrap(~ response, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +   labs(x = "Month", y = NULL)

code: set.seed(11) n_sp <- 4 n_year <- 20 n_visit <- 5 species <- paste0("sp_", seq_len(n_sp))  # A yearly temperature index with mean 0 and SD 1 temp <- round(as.numeric(scale(   cumsum(rnorm(n_year, 0, 0.6)) + rnorm(n_year) )), 2)  # AR(1) deviations in log abundance that temperature leaves unexplained z <- matrix(0, n_year, n_sp) for (t in 2:n_year) z[t, ] <- 0.6 * z[t - 1, ] + rnorm(n_sp, 0, 0.2)  # Each species' response to temperature on the log scale: a # saturating rise, a hump, a decline and a weak U temp_effect <- cbind(   0.8 * tanh(1.5 * temp),   0.6 - 0.6 * temp^2,   -0.5 * temp,   0.2 * temp^2 - 0.2 )  # Abundance N each year, around baselines of 30, 12, 20 and 10 log_lambda <- sweep(temp_effect + z, 2, log(c(30, 12, 20, 10)), "+") N <- matrix(rpois(n_year * n_sp, exp(log_lambda)), n_year, n_sp)  # Logit detection intercept of each species det_sp <- rnorm(n_sp, 0.3, 0.4)  # One row per visit, with wind speed recorded on each dat <- expand.grid(visit = seq_len(n_visit), time = seq_len(n_year),                    series = factor(species, levels = species)) dat$temp <- temp[dat$time] dat$wind <- round(runif(nrow(dat)), 2) dat$N <- N[cbind(dat$time, as.integer(dat$series))]  # Each individual present is counted with probability p, which falls # with wind speed p <- plogis(det_sp[dat$series] - 1.5 * dat$wind) dat$y <- rbinom(nrow(dat), dat$N, p)  # Upper bound of the sum over N in each closure unit dat$cap <- 80L head(dat) #>   visit time series temp wind  N  y cap #> 1     1    1   sp_1 1.07 0.77 59 25  80 #> 2     2    1   sp_1 1.07 0.14 59 31  80 #> 3     3    1   sp_1 1.07 0.50 59 28  80 #> 4     4    1   sp_1 1.07 0.04 59 47  80 #> 5     5    1   sp_1 1.07 0.36 59 27  80 #> 6     1    2   sp_1 1.56 0.20 48 21  80 train <- subset(dat, time <= 17) test <- subset(dat, time > 17)

code: set.seed(42) n_site <- 40 n_season <- 10 n_visit <- 4  # Forest cover of each site, with mean 0 and SD 1 forest <- round(as.numeric(scale(runif(n_site))), 2)  # Regional AR(1) deviations in logit occupancy, shared by every site z <- numeric(n_season) z[1] <- rnorm(1, 0, 0.6) for (t in 2:n_season) z[t] <- 0.7 * z[t - 1] + rnorm(1, 0, 0.45)  # Occupancy rises with forest cover and levels off f_forest <- function(x) 1.6 * tanh(1.2 * x) psi <- plogis(outer(f_forest(forest), z, "+") - 0.2) occupied <- matrix(rbinom(length(psi), 1, psi), n_site, n_season)  # One row per visit, with rain recorded on each dat <- expand.grid(visit = seq_len(n_visit), time = seq_len(n_season),                    site = seq_len(n_site)) dat$series <- factor("species1") dat$site <- factor(dat$site) dat$forest <- forest[as.integer(dat$site)] dat$rain <- round(runif(nrow(dat)), 2) dat$occupied <- occupied[cbind(as.integer(dat$site), dat$time)]  # An occupied site is detected with probability p, which falls with # rain. An empty site is never detected. p <- plogis(0.5 - 2 * dat$rain) dat$y <- rbinom(nrow(dat), 1, dat$occupied * p) head(dat) #>   visit time site   series forest rain occupied y #> 1     1    1    1 species1   1.07 0.39        1 1 #> 2     2    1    1 species1   1.07 0.08        1 1 #> 3     3    1    1 species1   1.07 0.83        1 0 #> 4     4    1    1 species1   1.07 0.07        1 1 #> 5     1    2    1 species1   1.07 0.11        0 0 #> 6     2    2    1 species1   1.07 0.64        0 0 train <- subset(dat, time <= 8) test <- subset(dat, time > 8) histories <- aggregate(y ~ site + time + forest, data = train, FUN = sum) histories$site <- reorder(histories$site, histories$forest) ggplot(histories, aes(x = time, y = site, fill = factor(y))) +   geom_tile(colour = "white") +   scale_fill_manual(     values = c("grey92", "#DCBCBC", "#C79999", "#A25050", "#7C0000"),     name = "Detections"   ) +   scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:8, expand = c(0, 0)) +   labs(x = "Season", y = "Site (ordered by forest cover)") +   theme(axis.text.y = element_blank(), axis.ticks.y = element_blank()) seen <- aggregate(y ~ site + forest + time, data = train, FUN = max) by_site <- aggregate(y ~ site + forest, data = seen, FUN = mean) ggplot(by_site, aes(x = forest, y = y)) +   geom_point(size = 2, alpha = 0.7) +   labs(x = "Forest cover (standardised)",        y = "Proportion of seasons with a detection")

code: set.seed(2025) n_months <- 120 # Rows hold this month's processes, columns last month's A <- rbind(prey     = c(0.6, -0.5),            predator = c(0.4,  0.5)) z <- matrix(0, n_months, 2) for (t in 2:n_months) {   z[t, ] <- A %*% z[t - 1, ] + rnorm(2, sd = 0.35) } predator_prey <- data.frame(   time = rep(seq_len(n_months), 2),   series = factor(rep(c("prey", "predator"), each = n_months),                   levels = c("prey", "predator")),   y = rpois(2 * n_months, exp(c(2.5 + z[, 1], 1.5 + z[, 2]))) ) mod_var <- mvgam(   y ~ series,   trend_formula = ~ VAR(),   data = predator_prey,   family = poisson(),   chains = 4, cores = 4, silent = 2 ) A_post <- posterior_transition_matrix(mod_var) plot(A_post) irfs <- irf(mod_var, h = 12) plot(irfs, series = 1) plot(irfs, series = 2) fevds <- fevd(mod_var, h = 12) plot(fevds)

text: state-space dataset three coral reefs surveyed irregular monthly intervals (gap distribution Uniform(1, 6) months, mean approximately 3.5). survey inspects 20 40 colonies counts bleached. latent state continuous-time AR(1) (CAR(1)) trend per reef phi = 0.9 sigma = 0.3 logit scale. observation equation adds observed sea-surface temperature (SST) driver smooth nonlinear effect.

title: Simulated coral bleaching surveys with an irregular CAR(1) state — coral_surveys
text: data.frame 150 rows following fields: series factor identifying reef (flynn, myrmidon, pixie); duplicated reef. time integer month index (irregularly spaced within reef). y integer count bleached colonies; duplicated bleaching. reef factor, alias series. sst numeric observed sea-surface temperature degrees Celsius. bleaching integer count bleached colonies, alias y. colonies integer number colonies inspected, binomial trials.

title: Simulated coral bleaching surveys with an irregular CAR(1) state — coral_surveys
text: naive AR(1) treats every consecutive survey one step. gives one-month gap six-month gap persistence. trend_formula = ~ CAR() supplied time column decays state length gap. ar1_trend measures persistence median gap surveys, three months . simulated value 0.9^3 = 0.73. True generative components, logit scale: intercept -0.85, puts typical survey near 30% bleached. reef adds centred intercept. Latent CAR(1) state per reef phi = 0.9 sigma = 0.3, propagated trend[t] = phi^dt * trend[t-1] + N(0, sigma * sqrt((1 - phi^(2*dt)) / (1 - phi^2))). Shared smooth nonlinear effect SST, evaluated thin-plate basis. Binomial observations: bleaching ~ Binomial(colonies, p).

code: # \dontrun{ # Ten years of monthly counts of a prey species and its predator. # Predators suppress the prey a month later. Prey raise the # predators a month later. set.seed(2025) n_months <- 120 A <- rbind(prey     = c(0.6, -0.5),            predator = c(0.4,  0.5)) z <- matrix(0, n_months, 2) for (t in 2:n_months) {   z[t, ] <- A %*% z[t - 1, ] + rnorm(2, sd = 0.35) } predator_prey <- data.frame(   time = rep(seq_len(n_months), 2),   series = factor(rep(c("prey", "predator"), each = n_months),                   levels = c("prey", "predator")),   y = rpois(2 * n_months, exp(c(2.5 + z[, 1], 1.5 + z[, 2]))) ) var_mod <- mvgam(y ~ series, trend_formula = ~ VAR(),                  data = predator_prey, family = poisson(),                  chains = 2, silent = 2) # } # \dontrun{ # The share of each series' forecast-error variance due to each # shock, over an eight-step horizon fevd_obj <- fevd(var_mod, h = 8L) plot(fevd_obj)   # Next: irf() traces each shock through the system over time # }

Its prior # table marks the replaced rows as "user". pre <- mvgam(y ~ s(x, k = 5), trend_formula = ~ AR(p = 1),              data = dat, family = poisson(), prior = my_priors,              run_model = FALSE) prior_summary(pre) #>                   prior       class        coef group resp dpar nlpar lb ub tag #>  student_t(3, 1.4, 2.5)   Intercept                                             #>            std_normal()           b                                             #>            std_normal()           b        sx_1                                 #>    student_t(3, 0, 2.5)         sds                                    0        #>    student_t(3, 0, 2.5)         sds s(x, k = 5)                        0        #>         inv_gamma(5, 1) sigma_trend                                    0        #>       normal(0.5, 0.25)   ar1_trend                                   -1  1     #>        source #>       default #>          user #>  (vectorized) #>       default #>  (vectorized) #>          user #>          user  # Next, drop `run_model = FALSE` to fit the model under these priors # }

code: # \dontrun{ set.seed(13) simdat <- sim_mvgam(family = poisson(), n_series = 1L,                      n_timepoints = 120L, trend_model = AR()) mod <- mvgam(y ~ s(x, k = 5), trend_formula = ~ AR(p = 1),               data    = simdat$data_train,               family  = poisson(),               chains  = 2, silent = 2) #> Warning: 8 of 2000 (0.0%) transitions ended with a divergence. #> See https://mc-stan.org/misc/warnings for details.  # The equations, glossary and priors as Markdown md <- methods_md(mod) md #> ## Data #>  #> $y$: non-negative integer counts #>  #> $N = 90$ observations, $S = 1$ series, $T = 90$ time points #>  #> Predictors: #>  #> - $x$: continuous covariate #>  #> ## Model #>  #> $$ #> \begin{aligned} #> t &\in \{1, \ldots, 90\} \\ #> y_{i,t} &\sim \text{Poisson}(\mu_{i,t}) \\ #> \log \mu_{i,t} &= \alpha + f_{x}(x_{i,t}) + \eta_{i,t} \\ #> f_{x}(x) &= \sum_{m=1}^{K_{x}} \beta^{(x)}_m B_m(x) \\ #> \eta_{i,t} &= \phi_{1} \eta_{i,t-1} + \epsilon^{(\eta)}_{i,t} \\ #> \epsilon^{(\eta)}_{i,t} &\sim \text{Normal}(0, \sigma_\eta) #> \end{aligned} #> $$ #>  #> where: #>  #> - $i$ indexes series, $t$ indexes time #> - $\mu_{i,t}$: conditional mean of $y_{i,t}$ #> - $\alpha$: population intercept #> - $f_{x}$: thin plate regression spline in $x$, basis size $K_{x} = 5$, smoothing SD $\sigma^{(s)}_{x}$ #> - $\eta_{i,t}$: latent state of series $i$ at time $t$ #> - $\epsilon^{(\eta)}_{i,t}$: process innovation, SD $\sigma_\eta$ #> - $\phi_{l}$: autoregressive coefficient at lag $l$ #>  #> ## Priors #>  #> $$ #> \begin{aligned} #> \alpha &\sim \text{StudentT}(3, 1.6, 2.5) \\ #> \sigma^{(s)}_{x} &\sim \text{StudentT}(3, 0, 2.5) \\ #> \sigma_\eta &\sim \text{InvGamma}(3, 1.07) \\ #> \phi_{1} &\sim \text{Normal}(0, 0.5) #> \end{aligned} #> $$ #>  #> Every other parameter takes an improper flat prior on its support. #>  #> ## Implementation #>  #> Fitted with mvgam 2.0.0.9000 (brms 2.23.2; Stan 2.40.0 via cmdstanr). Hamiltonian Monte Carlo: 2 chains, 1000 warmup + 1000 sampling iterations per chain. #>  #> ``` #> mvgam( #>   formula       = y ~ s(x, k = 5), #>   trend_formula = ~AR(p = 1), #>   data          = simdat$data_train, #>   family        = poisson(), #>   backend       = "cmdstanr", #>   chains        = 2, #>   iter          = 2000, #>   warmup        = 1000 #> ) #> ```  # Written to a file, nested under a level-two heading methods_md(mod, file = tempfile(fileext = ".md"), heading_level = 3L)  # Next, forecast(mod) predicts the times after the training data # }

title: mvgam: Multivariate (Dynamic) Generalized Additive Models — mvgam-package

The error names the column, the values and the support. counts <- simdat$data_train counts$y[3L] <- -1 try(mvgam_data(counts, family = poisson(), plot = FALSE)) #> Error : 'y' has values outside the support of family 'poisson'. #>   Requires: 0 <= 'y' (integers only). #>   Observed range: [-1, 26]. 1 of 135 values fall outside, the first at row #>   3. #>   Check the column for missing-data sentinels such as -1 or -999.  # AR() assumes evenly spaced times. For each parameter, Bulk_ESS #> and Tail_ESS are effective sample size measures, and Rhat is the potential #> scale reduction factor on split chains (at convergence, Rhat = 1). #>  #> Next steps: #>   - `pp_check(fit)`: posterior predictive checks #>   - `forecast(fit, newdata = ...)`: out-of-sample forecasts #>   - `lfo_cv(fit)`: leave-future-out model comparison #>   - `conditional_effects(fit)`: covariate effects #> Use `how_to_cite(fit)` for a methods paragraph and `methods_md(fit)` for its equations. #>  #> Multiple imputation: 3 fits of 2000 draws each, pooled. #> Rhat is each parameter's largest and each ESS its sum over the fits. #>    Imputation Max_Rhat Min_Bulk_ESS Min_Tail_ESS #>             1    1.006          460          736 #>             2    1.013          453          849 #>             3    1.005          580          810  # Next, `combine = FALSE` returns the three fits as a list # }

title: Multivariate normal family for several continuous responses — mvn
text: continuous responses measured together unit, biomass several species site. data hold one row per response component unit. Latent factors shared unit's components give residuals covariance Z Z' + diag(Psi^2), Z holds factor loadings Psi component's residual standard deviation (Hui et al. 2015; Niku et al. 2019). Given factors, row normal mean mu standard deviation Psi.

title: Multivariate normal family for several continuous responses — mvn
text: jsdgam() fits family, taking unit component columns number factors n_lv. residual_cor() summarises residual correlations shared_variation() part factors share. Psi takes prior inv_gamma(3, 1.07), median 0.40 mass zero, suits responses near unit scale. prior(..., class = Psi) sets another. K components data separate factor part residual part (K - n_lv)^2 >= K + n_lv. Fewer factors components meet bound. jsdgam() warns fails.

title: Multivariate Student-t family for several continuous responses — mvt
text: mvn() heavy-tailed residuals. Given latent factors, row follows Student-t distribution location mu, scale Psi degrees freedom nu, every component shares. outlying row pulls less fit. residual covariance Z Z' + diag(Psi^2 * nu / (nu - 2)). unit's responses follow multivariate Student-t law. factors stay normal.

text: counts made repeated visits sites whose abundance stays fixed across visits, bird point counts within season. data hold one row per visit. visits sharing series time belong one closure unit, whose latent abundance N Poisson mean mu. visit's count depends N detection parameter p. likelihood sums N unit's largest count cap K_max (Royle 2004).

title: N-mixture family for repeated counts of unmarked individuals — nmix
text: three variants take N ~ Poisson(mu) differ visit records. "poisson_binomial" (Royle 2004) Counts y ~ Binomial(N, p), never exceed N. Point counts, removal passes plot tallies fit design. p detection probability individual, logit link. "royle_nichols" (Royle Nichols 2003) Detections y ~ Bernoulli(1 - (1 - p)^N) 0 / 1. Camera-trap eDNA detections scored present absent fit design. p detection probability individual, logit link. visit's detection probability rises N. "poisson_poisson" (Neyman 1939) Counts y ~ Poisson(N * p), can exceed N. Camera-trap events acoustic detections, one individual recorded several times, fit design. p encounter rate individual per visit, log link.

title: N-mixture family for repeated counts of unmarked individuals — nmix
text: detection probability p logit link takes beta(1, 1) scalar. formula, intercept takes normal(0, 1.5), puts probability 0.05 0.95. encounter rate "poisson_poisson" takes lognormal(0, 1) scalar. formula, intercept takes std_normal(). Either puts rate 0.14 7.4 encounters per visit. get_prior() lists defaults. prior(..., dpar = "p") replaces one. rare species might take prior(normal(-2, 0.5), class = Intercept, dpar = "p").

title: N-mixture family for repeated counts of unmarked individuals — nmix
text: counts identify abundance detection apart repeated visits covariates act one . one visit per unit covariate, data identify product mu * p. nmix() refuses model. 30% units visited raises warning. "poisson_poisson" model intercepts alone separates mu p extra variance counts. warns. informative prior one intercept separates . Overdispersed abundance, negative binomial counts fitted Poisson N, biases abundance detection , leaving product close truth (Knape et al. 2018). pp_check() type = "fit_stat" tests per-unit totals misfit.

title: N-mixture family for repeated counts of unmarked individuals — nmix

"royle_nichols" takes fixed 25, unmarked::occuRN() . 0 / 1 detections carry count build cap . lower cap shortens sum speeds sampling. cap binds biases abundance . latent_N_saturation() reports, unit, posterior probability N equals cap. prediction frame may carry cap.

code: # \dontrun{ # Ten years of monthly counts of a prey species and its predator. # Predators suppress the prey a month later. Prey raise the # predators a month later. set.seed(2025) n_months <- 120 A <- rbind(prey     = c(0.6, -0.5),            predator = c(0.4,  0.5)) z <- matrix(0, n_months, 2) for (t in 2:n_months) {   z[t, ] <- A %*% z[t - 1, ] + rnorm(2, sd = 0.35) } predator_prey <- data.frame(   time = rep(seq_len(n_months), 2),   series = factor(rep(c("prey", "predator"), each = n_months),                   levels = c("prey", "predator")),   y = rpois(2 * n_months, exp(c(2.5 + z[, 1], 1.5 + z[, 2]))) ) var_mod <- mvgam(y ~ series, trend_formula = ~ VAR(),                  data = predator_prey, family = poisson(),                  chains = 2, silent = 2) # } # \dontrun{ # Each series' persistence and its effects on the others A <- posterior_transition_matrix(var_mod) A #> Lag-1 VAR transition matrix from an mvgam fit #>   Group      : single-panel #>   Dimension  : 2 x 2 #>   Mean |A_ij| (i != j): 0.53 #>   Point estimate: #>          prey predator #> prey     0.44    -0.58 #> predator 0.47     0.50 #>   95% CI on each cell available in `A_lower` / `A_upper`. plot(A)   # Next, irf(var_mod) traces how a shock to one series spreads # }

title: Calculate measures of latent VAR community stability — stability.mvgam
text: measures describe much lagged interactions among series contribute variability system. also describe system responds perturbation (Ives et al. 2003). latent VAR(1) $$   x_t \sim \text{MVNormal}(x_{t - 1}, \Sigma)   $$ stationary covariance \(\Sigma_{\infty}\) solves \(\Sigma_{\infty} = \Sigma_{\infty} ^\top + \Sigma\). posterior draw \(\) \(\Sigma\) gives one draw every metric: prop_int: proportion volume stationary distribution lagged interactions generate, \(\det()^2\).   prior \(\) keeps every draw stationary (Heaps 2023). \(\Sigma_{\infty}\) every metric exist every draw. irf() fevd() describe dynamics responses shocks.
code: \item `prop_int_adj`: `prop_int` scaled by the number of series \eqn{p}, \eqn{|\det(A)|^{2/p}}. It compares across systems of different size.  \item `prop_int_offdiag`, `prop_int_diag`: the sensitivity of `prop_int` to each cell of \eqn{A} is \eqn{2 \det(A) (A^{-1})^\top}. `prop_int_offdiag` is the mean absolute sensitivity of the off-diagonal cells (interactions between series) as a share of that mean plus the mean absolute sensitivity of the diagonal cells (self-regulation). `prop_int_diag` is the remaining share.  \item `prop_cov_offdiag`, `prop_cov_diag`: the same split for the sensitivity of \eqn{\det(\Sigma_{\infty})} to each cell of \eqn{\Sigma_{\infty}}, \eqn{\det(\Sigma_{\infty})     (\Sigma_{\infty}^{-1})^\top}. Off-diagonal cells are counted where \eqn{\Sigma} is estimated.  \item `reactivity`: the log of the largest singular value of \eqn{A}, \eqn{\log \sigma_{max}(A)} (Neubert et al. 2009). A positive value means some perturbation grows in the step after it occurs, before the system returns to equilibrium.  \item `mean_return_rate`: the largest modulus of the eigenvalues of \eqn{A}. The distance of the mean from its stationary value shrinks by this factor each step, asymptotically. A value nearer 1 means a slower return.  \item `var_return_rate`: the same factor for the variance, the largest modulus of the eigenvalues of \eqn{A \otimes A}, which is `mean_return_rate` squared.

code: # \dontrun{ # Ten years of monthly counts of a prey species and its predator. # Predators suppress the prey a month later. Prey raise the # predators a month later. set.seed(2025) n_months <- 120 A <- rbind(prey     = c(0.6, -0.5),            predator = c(0.4,  0.5)) z <- matrix(0, n_months, 2) for (t in 2:n_months) {   z[t, ] <- A %*% z[t - 1, ] + rnorm(2, sd = 0.35) } predator_prey <- data.frame(   time = rep(seq_len(n_months), 2),   series = factor(rep(c("prey", "predator"), each = n_months),                   levels = c("prey", "predator")),   y = rpois(2 * n_months, exp(c(2.5 + z[, 1], 1.5 + z[, 2]))) ) var_mod <- mvgam(y ~ series, trend_formula = ~ VAR(),                  data = predator_prey, family = poisson(),                  chains = 2, silent = 2) # } # \dontrun{ # Posterior medians and intervals of the stability metrics stab <- stability(var_mod) stab[stab$metric %in% c("reactivity", "mean_return_rate"), ] #>             metric   Estimate  Est.Error       Q2.5      Q97.5 #> 7       reactivity -0.1869083 0.11872230 -0.4362667 0.06179284 #> 8 mean_return_rate  0.7000529 0.06670612  0.5477350 0.81776418  # The full posterior of each metric plot(stability(var_mod, summary = FALSE))   # Next: irf() traces a shock through the system over time # }

title: Latent trend models for mvgam — print.mvgam_trend
code: # \dontrun{ # A constructor records a trend before any data are seen. Printing # one shows the settings the model will use AR(p = c(1, 12)) #> mvgam trend specification: #>   Type: AR({1, 12}) #>   Time variable: time #>   Series variable: series VAR(p = 2, ma = TRUE) #> mvgam trend specification: #>   Type: VARMA(2, 1) #>   Time variable: time #>   Series variable: series #>   Correlated innovations RW(gr = region, subgr = species) #> mvgam trend specification: #>   Type: RW #>   Time variable: time #>   Series variable: series #>   Correlated innovations #>   Hierarchical grouping: region #>   Subgroups: species  # A regularly spaced series usually starts with AR(p = 1). ?mvgam # fits one. The rest of this example handles irregular sampling.  # Three Poisson series with a seasonal cycle, each surveyed at its # own irregular times. sim_mvgam(type = 6L) draws the gaps between # occasions. Every series keeps about 60 percent of the occasions set.seed(11) simdat <- sim_mvgam(type = 6L, family = poisson(), n_series = 3L,                     n_timepoints = 80L) keep_some <- function(d) d[runif(nrow(d)) < 0.6, ] own_times <- keep_some(simdat$data_train)  # The parameters a trend adds, with their default priors, before # any fitting get_prior(   mvgam_formula(y ~ s(season, bs = "cc", k = 6),                 trend_formula = ~ CAR(cor = TRUE)),   data   = own_times,   family = poisson() ) #>                   prior         class                        coef group resp #>  student_t(3, 1.6, 2.5)     Intercept                                        #>    student_t(3, 0, 2.5)           sds                                        #>    student_t(3, 0, 2.5)           sds s(season, bs = "cc", k = 6)            #>      inv_gamma(3, 1.07)   sigma_trend                                        #>          normal(0, 0.5)     ar1_trend                                        #>    lkj_corr_cholesky(2) L_Omega_trend                                        #>  dpar nlpar    lb    ub tag       source #>                                  default #>                 0                default #>                 0           (vectorized) #>                 0                default #>             0.001 0.999          default #>                                  default  # A continuous-time AR(1) steps each series over its own gaps mod <- mvgam(   y ~ s(season, bs = "cc", k = 6),   trend_formula = ~ CAR(cor = TRUE),   data          = own_times,   family        = poisson(),   chains        = 2,   silent        = 2 ) #> Warning: 2 of 2000 (0.0%) transitions ended with a divergence. #> See https://mc-stan.org/misc/warnings for details. summary(mod) #>  Family: poisson  #>   Links: mu = log  #> Formula: y ~ s(season, bs = "cc", k = 6)  #>    Data: own_times (Number of observations: 109)  #>  Series: 3  #>  Trends: CAR  #>   Draws: 2 chains, each with iter = 2000; warmup = 1000; thin = 1;  #>          total post-warmup draws = 2000 #>  #> == Observation Model == #> Smoothing Spline Hyperparameters: #>                Estimate Est.Error l-95% CI u-95% CI Rhat Bulk_ESS Tail_ESS #> sds(sseason_1)     1.52      0.68     0.69     3.44 1.00      923     1338 #>  #> Regression Coefficients: #>           Estimate Est.Error l-95% CI u-95% CI Rhat Bulk_ESS Tail_ESS #> Intercept     1.58      0.09     1.40     1.74 1.00     1739     1588 #>  #> == Trend Model == #> Trend Specific Parameters: #>                       Estimate Est.Error l-95% CI u-95% CI Rhat Bulk_ESS #> sigma_trend[series_1]     0.32      0.09     0.17     0.51 1.00      981 #> sigma_trend[series_2]     0.47      0.12     0.26     0.73 1.00     1097 #> sigma_trend[series_3]     0.57      0.12     0.38     0.83 1.00     1405 #> ar1_trend[series_1]       0.60      0.21     0.12     0.92 1.00      681 #> ar1_trend[series_2]       0.41      0.22     0.04     0.83 1.00      929 #> ar1_trend[series_3]       0.18      0.15     0.01     0.54 1.00     1621 #>                       Tail_ESS #> sigma_trend[series_1]     1175 #> sigma_trend[series_2]     1416 #> sigma_trend[series_3]     1526 #> ar1_trend[series_1]       1144 #> ar1_trend[series_2]       1248 #> ar1_trend[series_3]       1219 #>  #> Draws were sampled using sampling(NUTS). For each parameter, Bulk_ESS #> and Tail_ESS are effective sample size measures, and Rhat is the potential #> scale reduction factor on split chains (at convergence, Rhat = 1). #>  #> Next steps: #>   - `pp_check(fit)`: posterior predictive checks #>   - `residual_cor(fit)`: implied correlations among series #>   - `forecast(fit, newdata = ...)`: out-of-sample forecasts #>   - `lfo_cv(fit)`: leave-future-out model comparison #>   - `conditional_effects(fit)`: covariate effects #> Use `how_to_cite(fit)` for a methods paragraph and `methods_md(fit)` for its equations.  # Correlations among the series' latent states residual_cor(mod) #> Residual correlations from an mvgam fit #>   Source     : correlated innovations #>   Covariance : stationary #>   Series     : 3 #>   Mean |r_ij| (i != j): 0.21 [0.06, 0.41] #>   Pairs with prob_nonzero > 0.95: 0 / 3  # Residual checks. Each series has gaps of differing length. A # semivariogram by time lag replaces the ACF plot(mod, type = "residuals", series = 2)   # Each series is forecast at its own future times plot(forecast(mod, newdata = keep_some(simdat$data_test)),      series = 2)   # Counts near 150 pin each latent state down. Sampled centred, this # random walk ran about five times faster per effective draw n_t <- 60 big <- data.frame(time = 1:n_t, series = factor("s1"),                   y = rpois(n_t, exp(5 + cumsum(rnorm(n_t, 0, 0.1))))) mod_big <- mvgam(   y ~ 1,   trend_formula = ~ RW(centred = TRUE),   data          = big,   family        = poisson(),   chains        = 2,   silent        = 2 ) summary(mod_big) #>  Family: poisson  #>   Links: mu = log  #> Formula: y ~ 1  #>    Data: big (Number of observations: 60)  #>  Trends: RW  #>   Draws: 2 chains, each with iter = 2000; warmup = 1000; thin = 1;  #>          total post-warmup draws = 2000 #>  #> == Observation Model == #> Regression Coefficients: #>           Estimate Est.Error l-95% CI u-95% CI Rhat Bulk_ESS Tail_ESS #> Intercept     4.88      0.14     4.59     5.15 1.01      226      487 #>  #> == Trend Model == #> Trend Specific Parameters: #>                 Estimate Est.Error l-95% CI u-95% CI Rhat Bulk_ESS Tail_ESS #> sigma_trend[s1]     0.12      0.02     0.09     0.16 1.00      537      858 #>  #> Draws were sampled using sampling(NUTS). For each parameter, Bulk_ESS #> and Tail_ESS are effective sample size measures, and Rhat is the potential #> scale reduction factor on split chains (at convergence, Rhat = 1). #>  #> Next steps: #>   - `pp_check(fit)`: posterior predictive checks #>   - `forecast(fit, newdata = ...)`: out-of-sample forecasts #>   - `lfo_cv(fit)`: leave-future-out model comparison #> Use `how_to_cite(fit)` for a methods paragraph and `methods_md(fit)` for its equations.  # Next: hindcast() returns the fitted latent trends. The articles # under 'See Also' fit VAR, hierarchical and factor trends # }

title: mvgam 2.0.0
text: CRAN release: 2026-11-27 mvgam now builds models ‘brms’. observation model takes full ‘brms’ formula syntax. trend_formula specifies latent process. 1.1.x code needs rewriting. Start vignette("mvgam_overview") vignette("data"). articles work model class.

title: mvgam 2.0.0
text: Trend constructors go inside trend_formula, trend_formula = ~ AR(p = 1). n_lv trend_map arguments trend constructors Removed arguments: trend_model, use_lv, prior_simulation, return_model_data, save_all_pars, parallel Data model trend need factor series column, even one series Renamed families: nb() negbinomial(), student_t() student(), betar() Beta() default family gaussian(). jsdgam() defaults binomial() Removed functions, replacements: get_mvgam_priors() (get_prior()), plot_mvgam_*() (plot()), compare_mvgams() (loo_compare()), eval_mvgam() roll_eval_mvgam() (lfo_cv()), lv_correlations() (residual_cor()), add_residuals() (augment()), code() (stancode()), ppc() (pp_check()) gp() mo() replace GP(), dynamic(), s(bs = "moi"), s(bs = "mod") Renamed arguments: incl_autocor (trend_state), process_error (resample_innovations), centred (noncentred) Parameter names follow ‘brms’, summary(), coef(), fixef(). Trend parameters indexed series name, sigma_trend[DM] Posterior summaries default irf(), fevd(), stability(). Pass summary = FALSE draws mvgam longer re-exports te() ti(). series_to_mvgam() longer takes xts input sim_mvgam() built around named scenarios. series_to_mvgam() returns one data frame unless h train_prop given

title: mvgam 2.0.0
text: mvbind() mvbf() responses share one latent process. See multivariate integrated distribution model articles Imperfect detection occ() nmix(), multi-season variant. forecast(type = "latent_state") forecasts occupancy abundance. See occupancy N-mixture articles jsdgam() takes traits, trait slopes, phylogeny composition families (diri(), multi(), categ()). Summaries fit: species_effects(), community(), residual_cor(). See JSDM article New dynamics: moving average terms coefficient pooling AR() VAR(), hierarchical VARs, local linear trend LLT(), extended CAR(). See VAR hierarchical VAR articles Structured factor loadings loadings_prior. Tools interpret loadings: active_factors(), shared_variation(), compare_loadings(), ordinate(). See vignette("dfm") New families: tweedie(), beta_nb(), com_binomial() (mathematics @jbogomolovas2), mvn(), mvt() ‘brms’ post-processing methods work mvgam fits. Examples: posterior_predict(), log_lik(), update(), hypothesis(), bridge_sampler() forecast_uncertainty() splits forecast variance source horizon. compare_scores() compare_elpds() compare models. See forecast evaluation article Checks model data fitting prediction: mvgam_formula(), mvgam_data(), check_newdata() methods_md() writes model description. bibtex() extracts citation Fits ‘cmdstanr’ 1.0, drops cmdstan_model(compile = FALSE) pp_check() given group draws type’s _grouped variant, one panel per group (#49)
